reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and threads holidays through schedule-template, parseRecurDate and getUpcomingDates, but the non-working-day predicate (isNonWorkingDay) stays private, so the server code rebuilds it from d.isWeekend plus isHoliday.

duplication.why: The daily-skip rule (daily + skipWeekend + weekend-or-holiday) is written three times: a while loop in getNextDate, a negated filter in getUpcomingDates and an if/continue in getDatesInRange; the schedule-template adjustWeekend closure does remove a local duplicate.

placement.why: The weekend/holiday move lives in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip decision is spread across the shared module and two server handlers instead of living beside the move rule.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; the getNextDate edit leaves mis-indented code, but nothing unrelated is touched.

maintainability.why: Three diverging copies of the skip rule, an odd holidays ? isNonWorkingDay : d.isWeekend ternary in getNextDate, a frequency !== 'DAILY' guard wrapped around the helper call, and a holidays.length + 2 search window heuristic make the rule hard to change safely.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts decide the daily skip with their own (d.isWeekend || isHoliday) conditions instead of a shared schedule rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily weekend/holiday skip appears reshaped as a while-advance loop (getNextDate), a .filter(!(...)) (getUpcomingDates) and a for/continue (getDatesInRange).

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a DAILY skip loop with a holidays-present ternary and a frequency !== 'DAILY' guard around the helper; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement the daily skip test.
